body.p: In the Office Action, claims 4 and 5 were objected to because of informalities. Applicant has amended claim 4 as suggested by the Examiner, and withdrawal of the objection to claims 4 and 5 is respectfully requested.

Claims 1-3, 6-7 and 11 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(1) as being anticipated by Martino Gonzalez (US 2008/0099611 Al). Claims 4-5 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Martino Gonzalez in view of Chavignier et al. (US 2016/00229546 Al). Additionally, claims 8-10 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Martino Gonzalez in view of Remy et al. (US 8,056,344 B2). Claim 12 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Martino Gonzalez in view of Mahioub (US 2006/0196633 Al). Finally, claim 13 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Martino Gonzalez in view of Chavignier. Applicant respectfully traverses the foregoing and requests reconsideration.

Notwithstanding the foregoing, solely in an effort to expedite prosecution, Applicant has amended claim 1 to recite "A hydrogen duct system arrangement for an aircraft, comprising: a hydrogen duct system installation mounted on an outside of a fuselage of the aircraft, and a variable fairing for covering the hydrogen duct system installation, wherein the fairing comprises at least one fairing body to be mounted on the outside of the fuselage." This amendment is supported by the Specification and adds no new matter. See claims 2 and 8; Published Application FIG. 1.

The Examiner acknowledges that Martino Gonzalez fails to disclose a hydrogen duct system installation as recited in original claim 8, which has been incorporated into amended claim 1. See Office Action page 6. FIG. 3 of Martino Gonzalez shows "a conventional embodiment of said tail cone 2 on which a firewall bulkhead 5 safeguards the rest of the fuselage 4 against possible risks of fire." Martino Gonzalez 0102. As shown in FIG. 26, Martino Gonzalez discloses a "movable fairing 9 [which] is comprised

of a primary lateral movable fairing 39 and a secondary lateral movable fairing 40." This movable fairing 9, "makes it possible to close and open the cover of the tail cone 2 and allows access to the auxiliary power unit 3." Martino Gonzalez 0106. Thus, Martino Gonzalez discloses a movable fairing 9 which is part of the fuselage, meaning it would be counterintuitive to modify Martino Gonzalez such that the fairing includes at least one fairing body to be mounted on the outside of the fuselage.

Remy fails to resolve the deficiencies of Martino Gonzalez. Remy discloses a hydrogen-injection arrangement 48 which "includes a source of gaseous hydrogen, here represented for example by gas containers 50, 51; hydrogen duct 52; and 65 second controllable valves 54 for closing and opening the hydrogen ducts 52." Remy Col. 5, lines 63-67. However, Remy fails to disclose or suggest a hydrogen duct system installation mounted on an outside of a fuselage of the aircraft. The other cited references similarly fail to disclose or suggest the features of claim 1.

Accordingly, the cited references fail to disclose or suggest all of the features of claim 1. Thus, claim 1 should be allowable over the cited art. Those claims that depend therefrom should be allowable as well-at least by virtue of their claim dependency.
Applicant respectfully submits that claims 14-16 are allowable over the cited references.

Applicant therefore respectfully submits that all of the claims of the application should be found to be allowable and thus requests that the Examiner indicate all of the claims as allowed and pass the application to allowance.

Furthermore, the fact that Applicant has only addressed certain rejections should not be considered to be acquiescence to the rejections. Rather, Applicant has presented the argument herein in an effort to expedite prosecution. Applicant reserves any and all rights to address any rejection made but not specifically addressed herein.
The Commissioner is hereby authorized to charge any additional fees which may be required to this application under 37 C.F.R. §§ 1.16-1.17, or credit any overpayment, to Deposit Account No. 07-2069.
Should the Examiner discover there are remaining issues which may be resolved by a telephone interview, the Examiner is invited to contact the undersigned attorney at (312) 600-6841.
